items.summary: Travel experts at Google Flights advise that the optimal time to purchase airfare for the Thanksgiving and Christmas 2026 holidays is between 21 and 57 days before departure. For Thanksgiving specifically, data indicates the lowest prices generally occur 34 days before the flight date, though fares fluctuate daily based on demand.
items.title: Google Flights Identifies Best Window for Cheap Holiday Airfare

items.summary: Residents in Newport and Cardiff oppose new hyperscale datacentres, citing noise, air pollution, and health risks from gas turbines and diesel generators. Dale Johnston and Greg Pirio describe degraded quality of life, while campaigners like Owen Espley note growing grassroots resistance across the UK. The Labour government supports the expansion as essential for AI growth, establishing five AI zones and viewing it as an inevitable revolution. However, anti-datacentre groups argue the industry imposes resource-hungry, polluting operations with little local benefit. In Cardiff, a proposed facility faces 1,200 planning objections and a halt order from the Plaid Cymru-led government. Despite developer claims of regulatory compliance, concerns persist over emissions and grid strain, with some residents threatening to move or vote against representatives.
items.title: Residents Clash with Datacentre Expansion in Wales

items.summary: Becky Barnicoat is the subject of a cartoon titled 'Becky Barnicoat on scary outfits for Halloween.' The item presents this title as the sole content, offering no further details, quotes, or claims regarding the cartoon's specific content or Barnicoat's statements.
items.title: Becky Barnicoat Discusses Scary Outfits for Halloween in Cartoon

items.summary: Gritt Robotics is deploying AI-assisted robotic systems to address a shrinking solar workforce. The company recently announced deployments at sites run by EPC Burns & McDonnell and is working with three top-10 solar EPCs to install six million panels with a capacity of about 2.8 GW over the next two years. CEO Puneet Puri notes that solar sites offer a combination of regularity and variability suitable for automation. Industry reports indicate a shortfall of 53,000 workers needed for ongoing projects, with some estimates suggesting 41% of construction workers nationwide will retire by 2031. Gritt aims to apply lessons learned from solar construction to data centers and other infrastructure projects.
items.title: Gritt Robotics Deploys AI Systems to Address Solar Workforce Shortage

items.summary: Environmental groups launched a community science project to identify North Carolina poultry farms, which state law keeps confidential. Following a 2023 complaint about odors from Bladen County, volunteers analyzed satellite imagery to locate concentrated animal feeding operations. The project identified over 2,300 poultry and 2,000 swine facilities across six counties. Leaders note that while swine operations face a moratorium, poultry farms have doubled in some areas, raising concerns about air and water contamination from waste spread on fields.
items.title: Community Project Maps Secret North Carolina Poultry Farms

items.summary: An interview with Tzeporah Berman of the Fossil Fuel Non-Proliferation Treaty Initiative outlines efforts to establish a binding global treaty to phase out fossil fuels. Following a conference in Santa Marta, Colombia, that gathered 57 countries and the European Union, proponents aim to form a high-ambition coalition. Berman notes that approximately 25 countries are currently designing the treaty, with expectations that 35 to 40 nations will join once formal negotiations begin in 2027. The initiative seeks to complement the Paris Agreement by addressing supply reduction rather than just emissions. Berman cites the oil and gas industry's historical profits and lobbying as barriers, while highlighting endorsements from 4,000 organizations across 120 countries. The movement aims to shift social norms and foreign policy practices regarding fossil fuel production.
items.title: Activists Push for Global Fossil Fuel Treaty Outside UN Framework

items.summary: Italy installed 4.83 GW of new solar capacity between January and September 2026, according to data from industry association Italia Solare. This figure represents an increase from 4.08 GW in the same period of 2025. Utility-scale projects dominated the market, accounting for 46% of new capacity, while commercial and residential segments also recorded growth. Sicily led in capacity additions, whereas Lombardy topped the number of installations. Cumulative installed capacity reached 48.35 GW by the end of September 2026.
items.title: Italy Adds 4.83 GW of Solar Capacity in First Nine Months of 2026

items.summary: A report states the global energy transition requires 38.2 terawatts of renewable capacity by 2050, alongside stronger grids and efficiency. Current progress falls short of 1.5°C warming limits. Electrification is projected to rise from 23% to over 50% of final energy consumption by 2050. Renewable employment is expected to reach 84.2 million jobs by 2050. Coordinated investment in generation, transmission, and storage is deemed essential for a resilient, low-carbon system.
items.title: Global Energy Transition Needs Massive Renewable Capacity and Grid Upgrades

items.summary: Solidus Techno Power Private Limited announced the successful delivery of a 27.31 MWh Battery Energy Storage System integrated with a 50 MW solar project for SBF Ispat Private Limited. The company provided EPC services, marking a milestone in its renewable energy portfolio. CEO Jaspal Singh noted the system offers industries greater flexibility, while Managing Director Harvinder Singh highlighted the expansion of manufacturing capabilities through its subsidiary, XenRosh ESS.
items.title: Solidus Techno Power Delivers Integrated Solar and Storage System for SBF Ispat

items.summary: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra indicated that Tata Sons might need to list on stock exchanges if classified as an upper-layer NBFC. Speaking in New Delhi, he stated that such entities must register with the RBI due to associated operational and systemic risks, as reported by The Indian Express.
items.title: RBI Governor Says Tata Sons May Need to List as NBFC

items.summary: Indian service exporters, freelancers, and tech startups are protesting the Reserve Bank of India's new foreign exchange reporting framework, which took effect on October 1, 2026. The frustration stems from the mandatory Export Declaration Form (EDF), which extends rigorous compliance requirements previously limited to physical goods and major software vendors to independent consultants, content creators, SaaS firms, and small digital businesses.
items.title: Service Exporters Protest New RBI Foreign Exchange Reporting Rules

items.summary: Freelance journalist Emily Bratt argues that fining people who play audio without headphones in public, a policy proposed by Andy Burnham, is insufficient to address the root causes of antisocial behaviour. Drawing on her experience living in Japan between 2019 and 2021, Bratt suggests that British society needs to rebuild social norms and foster a sense of civic responsibility rather than relying solely on legislation. She highlights Japan's emphasis on avoiding inconvenience to others and school practices that teach personal responsibility for public spaces. Bratt warns that without enforcing rules and changing social attitudes, such fines may fail to curb the widespread issue of loudcasting in the UK.
items.title: Emily Bratt argues Britain should learn from Japan to tackle antisocial behaviour

items.summary: Little Stars, a Shropshire charity, expects high demand for its Santa's Little Stars campaign, which provides Christmas presents to struggling families. Running from late October to early December, the initiative accepts donations of new, unwrapped toys. The charity, which launched the campaign in 2020, has distributed over 8,000 presents to more than 2,100 children since then. Officials attribute the anticipated high demand to ongoing financial pressures faced by many families.
items.title: Little Stars Charity Anticipates High Demand for Christmas Campaign

items.summary: UK residents are stockpiling dried foods, bottled water, medicine, and power banks following government advice to prepare for various eventualities. Lawrence Barratt and Marco Camurri cited official warnings about Russian threats and climate crises, as well as memories of supply shortages during the 2020 lockdown, as motivations. Jack Davenport also noted El Niño and infrastructure concerns. Conversely, Deirdre O'Sullivan dismissed the guidance as inadequate and reminiscent of outdated 1970s advice. While the government launched a campaign on Thursday, ministers have been making similar noises for months, prompting some to begin preparations about a fortnight ago or several months prior.
items.title: UK Residents Stockpile Food and Supplies Amid Official Warnings

items.summary: Joe Weisenthal stated that the day Anthropic introduced Mythos marks 'The Red Line.' This comment appears in a text titled 'Cybersecurity ETF,' though the content focuses on Anthropic's product launch rather than the ETF itself.
items.title: Joe Weisenthal Identifies Mythos Launch as Anthropic's Red Line

items.summary: On September 26, 1983, Soviet Lieutenant Colonel Stanislav Petrov faced a false alarm from early-warning satellites indicating five American nuclear missiles were inbound. Despite the system's high reliability rating, Petrov correctly identified the signal as a malfunction rather than an attack. His decision to ignore the warning prevented a potential nuclear exchange, illustrating how human judgment can override automated systems in crisis situations.
items.title: Stanislav Petrov Avoided Nuclear War by Rejecting False Alarm

items.summary: An article from Reader's Digest highlights five allegedly haunted hotels in America, ranging from the 1886 Crescent Hotel in Arkansas to the Hotel Alex Johnson in South Dakota. The piece details specific legends, such as a stonemason's death at the Crescent Hotel and the 'Pink Lady' at the Omni Grove Park Inn in North Carolina. While the text notes that reports of hauntings are not proof of the supernatural, it emphasizes how these stories attract curious travelers seeking historic atmosphere and mystery. The hotels offer various experiences, from viewing ghost journals to participating in ghost tours, blending history with enduring paranormal claims.
items.title: Five Haunted Hotels in America Offer Spooky Stays for Curious Travelers

items.summary: Brazilian factories installed almost 4,300 industrial robots last year, representing a 38 percent increase over 2024 and the highest volume in a decade. Nearly half of these installations occurred at car plants. The International Federation of Robotics suggests that investment by Chinese carmakers is the most likely reason for this surge.
items.title: Chinese carmakers drive surge in robots on Brazilian factory floors

items.summary: Global cybersecurity experts are urging organizations to update their systems following the discovery of a vulnerability in the programming language that powers most of the internet. Two cybersecurity companies, Calif and Wiz, stated they used Artificial Intelligence agents to find the flaw. Consequently, several European government websites went offline on Wednesday as a precautionary measure.
items.title: Cybersecurity Experts Urge System Updates After AI-Discovered Flaw

items.summary: President Xi Jinping quoted Tang Dynasty poet Du Fu during a plenary session of the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection on January 12, 2016. The quote, "If we do not eradicate evil... our Party members and the people will lose their faith in us," underscores the importance of rooting out corruption to maintain public trust and political stability.
items.title: President Xi Jinping Quotes Du Fu on Eradicating Evil During Plenary Session

items.summary: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi stated at the 2026 Global Governance Forum that the China-proposed Global Governance Initiative has gained relevance. He urged countries to uphold the United Nations' central role and enhance Security Council capacity. The forum, held in Xiongan, gathered nearly 400 representatives from over 90 countries to discuss global governance reforms and cooperation in emerging fields.
items.title: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi Promotes Global Governance Initiative

items.summary: French police fired tear gas to disperse approximately 150 protesters gathered outside Lyon 3 University on Saturday, 24 October. The demonstration occurred in a zone where protests were banned, amidst high tensions across France following a weekend of unrest involving clashes, arson, and looting. Authorities have tightened security measures in prohibited areas to prevent a repeat of the destruction seen last weekend.
items.title: French Police Use Tear Gas to Disperse Protesters in Lyon

items.summary: Protests have begun across France and Italy, with thousands expected in Orléans and Milan. French authorities have restricted routes and increased policing following recent riots and a deadly shooting. Demonstrators oppose right-wing leaders and demand social reforms, while police prepare for potential disorder.
items.title: Protests erupt across France and Italy amid political tensions and recent violence

items.summary: Singapore's Ministry of Manpower is investigating Process Maintenance Solutions and Jurong Technical & Construction for unpaid salaries owed to migrant workers. NTUC's Desmond Choo noted close to 240 workers in the sector have gone without pay for up to two months. MOM confirmed awareness of the arrears and stated it is working with support agencies to assist affected workers with claims and immediate needs.
items.title: Singapore investigates two firms over unpaid migrant worker salaries

items.summary: Bayern Munich sporting director Max Eberl stated that manager Vincent Kompany remains in stable condition after collapsing during reserve-team training but will be sidelined for weeks. Kompany, 40, had been battling a virus. Eberl emphasized that recovery time is measured in weeks, not days, and the club will prioritize his health before discussing a return. Assistant coach Aaron Danks will lead the team against Freiburg.
items.title: Bayern Munich Manager Vincent Kompany Hospitalized and Sidelined for Weeks

items.summary: Eight people were killed and 40 injured when gunmen opened fire at a funeral at St George's Greek Orthodox church in Karak, Jordan. Authorities labeled the attack a terrorist act by extremists. The head of the Public Security Directorate stated that most injured persons are receiving treatment while the search for attackers continues. Jordan's King Abdullah vowed harsh retaliation, and the UN secretary general condemned the violence against civilians.
items.title: Gunmen Kill Eight and Injure 40 at Church Funeral in Jordan

items.summary: Euronews released a news bulletin on October 24th, 2026, offering a brief overview of global stories. The broadcast covers world affairs, business, politics, culture, entertainment, and travel. Described as independent and European, the program aims to provide a reliable context for viewers navigating a fast-paced day. It serves as a regular update on current events shaping the world.
items.title: Latest news bulletin | October 24th, 2026 – Midday

items.summary: WA Premier Roger Cook visited South Hedland, located 1,600 kilometres north of Perth, for the first time since a coronial inquest into the 2022 deaths of three children was announced. Residents confronted the premier and Child Protection Minister Jessica Stojkovski regarding reports that up to 15 children lived unsupervised in a state-owned home. While the government highlighted progress, including a selected contractor for a $22 million MRI facility, community elders urged deeper engagement. Opposition leader Basil Zempilas criticized the lack of meetings with affected families. The WA Commissioner for Children and Young People tabled a report with 56 recommendations following the deaths.
items.title: WA Premier Confronted by Community Over Child Protection Failures

items.summary: French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez warned police to remain mobile and responsive ahead of Saturday's demonstrations in Paris. He cited significant calls for disruption from political movements and criminal groups. Students and Yellow Vests protesters are expected to march over cost-of-living issues. Last week, an estimated 500,000 to 800,000 people demonstrated across France, resulting in more than 2,500 arrests.
items.title: French Interior Minister Urges Police Alertness Ahead of Paris Protests

items.summary: Kenya has recorded its second death from Ebola as it handles its first ever outbreak of the disease. A 65-year-old woman, a close family member of the first victim, died after being placed in quarantine, the health ministry said. Seven other patients are receiving treatment at two isolation facilities. All cases are within one cluster with no evidence of community spread, the ministry said.
items.title: Kenya Records Second Ebola Death Amid First Outbreak

items.summary: Seven people remain missing after a multi-storey building collapsed in Nairobi, trapping them under rubble while dozens of workers escaped unharmed. Rescue efforts face challenges as heavy machinery risks cutting off air to the trapped. The incident has sparked concerns about construction standards, with officials noting that the building lacked required paperwork and raising questions about whether it met planning regulations.
items.title: Seven Missing After Building Collapse in Nairobi Raises Construction Concerns

items.summary: The Saudi-led coalition reported intercepting and destroying two Houthi ballistic missiles aimed at the Saudi cities of Taif and Yanbu. Coalition spokesman Brig. Gen. Turki al-Maliki confirmed the interception on social media. The incident occurs amid escalating hostilities between the Houthis and the coalition, which includes attacks on Saudi airports and energy facilities.
items.title: Saudi-led coalition intercepts two Houthi missiles targeting Taif and Yanbu

items.summary: Ukraine's defence minister stated that Starlink and Starshield connections have returned to stable speeds exceeding 400km per hour. This follows over a week of restrictions that slowed speeds to about 160 kph or less, disrupting military operations. While monitoring systems indicate a return to normal, the ministry did not confirm full service restoration. Neither SpaceX nor the US government has acknowledged responsibility for the previous throttling.
items.title: Ukraine Reports Stable Starlink Connection After Disruptions

items.summary: The navy of Iran's Islamic Revolution Guard Corps stated that two supertankers attempting an unauthorized route south of the Strait of Hormuz struck naval mines and exploded on Friday. Carrying over 4.5 million barrels of crude, the vessels caught fire and were abandoned. Iran cited a prior security incident and claimed to have destroyed navigational aids to stop violating traffic. Separately, the UK Maritime Trade Operations reported an incident involving an outbound tanker struck by an unknown projectile in the same waterway.
items.title: Iran Claims Two Oil Tankers Struck in Strait of Hormuz

items.summary: A fire engulfed the Eagle's Nest, a former retreat for Adolf Hitler in the Bavarian Alps. German police have detained a suspect, with local media suggesting arson. Authorities stated the blaze was difficult to tackle due to the site's high altitude and remote location. No injuries were reported, and the building was found empty. The investigation remains ongoing.
items.title: Fire Breaks Out at Hitler's Eagle's Nest Retreat in Bavaria

items.summary: A clinical trial for the TUMAiNi Ebola vaccine candidate began in Bunia, Ituri Province, Democratic Republic of Congo, on Saturday. The trial evaluates vaccines against the Bundibugyo virus among contacts of confirmed cases. Major General Kasongo Gaby, governor of Ituri Province, stated the launch marks a significant moment in the fight against the outbreak. The trial is led by the National Institute for Biomedical Research with support from the World Health Organization. Since mid-May, the DRC has confirmed more than 9,000 cases, while Uganda reported 20 cases before being declared Ebola-free in August.
items.title: New Ebola Vaccine Trial Launches in Bunia Amid DRC Outbreak Struggles

items.summary: GMO Internet requested that the Japanese government implement active cyber defense operations following an unauthorized access incident affecting its FX currency margin trading servers. The company, which estimates up to 26,739 servers may be involved, plans to compensate users for losses and offer a ¥5,000 consolation payment to all affected accounts. Sources reported the incident on Saturday.
items.title: GMO Internet Urges Government for Active Cyber Defense After Breach

items.summary: Park24 announced a ¥3,000 consolation payment for Times Car users affected by a data breach compromising 6.62 million accounts. Approximately 1.46 million accounts had identification documents transferred. The company expects the total payment cost to reach ¥4.4 billion and plans an extraordinary loss of ¥5.5 billion. Makino Law Office plans a lawsuit, noting the payment is too low.
items.title: Park24 Announces Compensation for Times Car Data Breach Victims

items.summary: Scientists indicate that wetlands and dense forests in Poland's Białowieża Forest might function as natural military defenses. Simultaneously, these wetlands are described as a potential lifeline for the forest. In a separate context, the Belo Monte hydroelectric plant in the Brazilian Amazon faces a contentious environmental license renewal after ten years of operation. Debates focus on revising the dam's discharge into the Xingu River, as holding back up to 70% of the river flow is pushing water scarcity.
items.title: Can a swamp stop an army?

items.summary: Mikey Madison, the 27-year-old actress who won an Oscar for her role in 'Anora', has returned to the screen after an 18-month hiatus. She stars as Frances Haugen in Aaron Sorkin's 'The Social Reckoning', a role she chose not to meet with the real-life subject to preserve her creative vision. Madison, known for her reserved nature and background as a horse rider, remains selective about her projects while balancing her career with her personal life in Los Angeles. She is currently filming 'My Darling California' and preparing an adaptation of an Edgar Allan Poe story.
items.title: Mikey Madison Returns to Hollywood with New Oscar Role

items.summary: More than 200 AI-generated political ads have circulated in the United States during the midterm election cycle, with spending exceeding $100 million according to the Wesleyan Media Project. One example features a rival campaign using artificial intelligence to create an implausible video of Democratic candidate James Talarico rewriting the Book of Genesis. While experts note that many voters can detect these edits, the impact on voter behavior remains unknown. Currently, 31 states have varying laws regarding AI disclosures, but no federal legislation exists to regulate the practice uniformly.
items.title: AI-Generated Political Ads Proliferate in Midterms Amid Regulatory Uncertainty

items.summary: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra stated that India possesses sufficient foreign exchange reserves to meet repayment obligations for FCNR(B) deposits, even amidst global financial uncertainty. Speaking at a media summit, he expressed confidence in the nation's external sector and medium-term balance of payments outlook. Malhotra highlighted strong macroeconomic fundamentals, supported by services exports and sustained domestic activity, while noting that high-frequency indicators continue to signal growth momentum across multiple sectors.
items.title: RBI Governor Says India Has Enough Forex Reserves For FCNR(B) Repayments

items.summary: Gwalior police registered a case regarding the alleged rape and blackmail of a 17-year-old Class 12 student by a man she met on Instagram. The suspect, identified as Aarush Mishra, allegedly threatened the girl with death and shared secretly recorded videos with her relatives. Police launched a search for Mishra, who remains at large, while the victim has stopped attending coaching classes due to fear.
items.title: Gwalior Police Register Case After NEET Aspirant Allegedly Raped And Blackmailed By Instagram Friend

items.summary: In 1995, Jeff Bezos's parents, Jackie and Mike Bezos, invested $245,573 of their life savings into Amazon, betting on their son despite the uncertain future of online shopping. Bezos later testified that he warned them there was a 70% chance they would lose the money. The company grew from an online bookstore into a global giant, transforming the family's investment into a fortune estimated at $51.7 billion for Mike Bezos's remaining stake as of September 2026. The family also donated shares to the Bezos Family Foundation.
items.title: Jeff Bezos's Parents Bet Life Savings on Amazon in 1995

items.summary: Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman chaired the 30th meeting of the Financial Stability and Development Council in New Delhi on Friday, according to a Ministry of Finance social media post. The gathering included the RBI Governor, heads of key financial regulators, and senior government officials. The FSDC serves as the apex forum for discussing financial stability and sector development issues.
items.title: Finance Minister Sitharaman Chairs 30th FSDC Meeting in New Delhi

items.summary: A Union Bank of India research report forecasts that financing demand in India will shift toward battery storage, semiconductors, green hydrogen, and defence over the next three to five years. The report notes significant investment potential in these sectors but cautions lenders about risks like technology obsolescence and long payback periods, recommending specialised lending capabilities.
items.title: Union Bank of India Report Highlights Financing Shift to Emerging Sectors

items.summary: Congress leader Jairam Ramesh questioned the government's decision to release US national Matthew VanDyke, an accused in the Myanmar arms training case, while activists protesting alleged electoral irregularities remain detained. A Delhi court extended permission for VanDyke and six Ukrainian nationals to remain outside India until February 24, 2027, while the NIA continues its probe. Ramesh alleged the release contradicts the handling of domestic protests and criticized the government's actions.
items.title: Congress questions government decision to release US national in Myanmar arms case

items.summary: The article explores why some women uphold patriarchal norms, citing a 2008 statement by Mamata Banerjee and a viral 'Long Live Patriarchy' march. Experts like Devika Anand and Dolly Kumari suggest that women may internalize traditional roles due to upbringing, viewing them as values rather than restrictions. Anand notes that challenging these norms can feel like denying past sacrifices, while Kumari argues tradition need not imply oppression. Tai Savitri, a 65-year-old influencer, attributes the phenomenon to a lack of education and systemic pitting of women against each other. The piece concludes that defending patriarchy often stems from a desire for security, identity, or a belief in traditional stability, rather than a single cause.
items.title: Why Some Women Defend Patriarchy: Insights from Experts and Activists

items.summary: The Government of Singapore holds stakes in 36 Indian companies worth approximately Rs 1,26,299 crore as of October 24, 2026. Around 14 stocks in the portfolio delivered positive returns so far in FY27, with top performers gaining between 20% and 100%.
items.title: Singapore Govt India Portfolio Stocks Rally

items.summary: Vested Finance data identifies ten US stocks that fell between 49% and 66% year to date in 2026. The Trade Desk led losses at 65.75%, while others like Flutter Entertainment and Stellantis dropped over 62%. The article notes ongoing AI trade and geopolitical tensions as context for the pressure.
items.title: Ten US Stocks Lost Up to 66% of Value in 2026 Amid Market Pressure

items.summary: Samar Chavan, 19, allegedly stole 15 tolas of gold worth Rs 10 lakh from his uncle Umesh Chavan in Satve village, Kolhapur. He sold the jewellery with a goldsmith's help to buy a Mahindra Thar. After inviting Umesh for the car's puja, the uncle discovered the missing ornaments. Police arrested Chavan and the goldsmith following a probe into the sudden acquisition of funds.
items.title: Man Steals Uncle's Gold to Buy Car Then Invites Him for Puja

items.summary: Ponnam Ashok Goud, chair of the TPCC Legal Cell, stated that lawyers played a crucial role in establishing the People's government in 2023 and the Telangana State. During a meeting in Hyderabad, he emphasized the unforgettable contribution of legal professionals. Ponnam Prabhakar, BC Welfare Minister, added that the party will focus on providing opportunities, resolving issues, and offering legal advice to Congress-affiliated lawyers across the 33 districts of Telangana.
items.title: Ponnam Highlights Lawyers' Contribution to Telangana Statehood and Future Plans

items.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath announced a significant expansion of the state's cybersecurity and forensic infrastructure ahead of TechSangam 2026. He noted that while the state previously had only two cyber police stations and four forensic laboratories before 2017, it now has stations in all 75 districts. Adityanath emphasized that this growth aims to enhance public safety, justice, and youth employment opportunities through emerging technologies.
items.title: UP Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath Highlights Cybersecurity and Forensic Expansion

items.summary: Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis ordered a forensic probe into a controversial audio clip alleging that Deputy CM Eknath Shinde received Rs 500 crore from the BJP. The clip, released by activist Manoj Jarange, sparked accusations from Shiv Sena leader Ramdas Kadam that BJP insiders were plotting against Shinde. While Fadnavis committed to uncovering the truth, Jarange demanded an impartial Special Investigation Team (SIT) and raids, warning that failure to act would erode public confidence. Kadam also accused Jarange of colluding with the BJP to undermine Shinde, citing names of BJP leaders in the recording.
items.title: Maharashtra CM Orders Forensic Probe Amid Political Audio Controversy

items.summary: Police allege that shooters involved in the October 18 attack on actor Tiger Shroff in Mumbai received real-time updates based on media coverage to evade arrest. Handlers allegedly monitored news reports and sent messages instructing the accused to change locations and transport modes. The three main suspects, aged 18 and 22, were caught in Kota on October 19. Investigators are probing the use of encrypted apps like Signal and Zangi, noting that digital evidence showed frequent contact between the attackers and their handlers. Gangster Anil Pandit, an associate of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang, claimed responsibility for the firing.
items.title: Shooters Used Media Coverage to Evade Police in Tiger Shroff Attack

items.summary: Will Murray, an ABC reporter in Morayfield, and bystander Daniel Hainey rescued a driver whose four-wheel drive stalled and sank in floodwaters on Buchanan Road. Murray called Triple Zero while Hainey entered the water; both men opened the rear door to pull the driver to safety. Emergency services arrived ten minutes later. Murray credited rushing water pressure for opening the door. The Queensland Fire Department warns residents never to drive or swim in floodwaters.
items.title: ABC Reporter and Bystander Rescue Driver from Sinking SUV in Brisbane Flood

items.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps asserts full control over the Strait of Hormuz, alleging two oil supertankers struck naval mines on an unauthorized route. Major General Ali Abdollahi warned US warships against entering the Persian Gulf, stating Iranian forces have rendered the US Navy ineffective. While Iran maintains restrictions, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent reported oil exports from the region have risen above pre-conflict levels.
items.title: Iran Claims Control of Strait of Hormuz and Warns US

items.summary: Unusually warm Pacific waters reached 30°C, signaling a strengthening El Nino that may alter global weather. The World Meteorological Organization warns sea surface temperatures could rise significantly by late 2026. Experts caution that while this phenomenon historically risks below-normal monsoon rainfall in India, outcomes depend on other factors like the Indian Ocean Dipole. Officials advise assessing these projections alongside official forecasts from the India Meteorological Department.
items.title: Strengthening El Nino Raises Climate Concerns for India

items.summary: Jamia Millia Islamia announced an immediate shift to online classes as a precautionary measure amid student protests demanding the restoration of the students' union. The All India Students' Association alleged an assault on protesters and hunger strikers, noting the strike's 13th day. Students, including Jasim Ali Khan and Anas, continued demanding union restoration and the removal of the Chief Proctor, while addressing allegations regarding campus graffiti.
items.title: Jamia Millia Islamia shifts classes online amid student protests and hunger strike

items.summary: India condemned a deadly shooting at a Greek Orthodox church in Karak, Jordan, that killed eight people and injured 34 others on Friday. External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar and MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal expressed condolences to the victims' families and reaffirmed India's solidarity with the Jordanian government and people. The attack occurred during a funeral, with footage showing gunmen firing pistols and a rifle. While the death toll was initially reported as seven, Reuters later updated it to eight. Jordan's King Abdullah II vowed harsh penalties for the terrorist act. No group has claimed responsibility, and authorities are searching for the attackers.
items.title: India Condemns Deadly Church Attack in Jordan and Reaffirms Anti-Terrorism Stance

items.summary: Jamia Millia Islamia moved all courses online and cancelled its 106th Foundation Day celebrations due to student protests demanding the restoration of the Students' Union. The administration cited safety concerns, while the All India Students' Association alleged assaults on protesters. A hunger strike entered its 13th day as students continued to demand the reinstatement of their union and the removal of the chief proctor.
items.title: Jamia Millia Islamia shifts classes online amid student protests

items.summary: A fire broke out at Krishna Food Point, a hotel in Noida's Sector 125, on Saturday afternoon. The blaze spread to nearby eateries, causing panic. Firefighters deployed four vehicles and personnel from the Sector 126 police station brought the fire under control. No casualties were reported. The Gautam Budh Nagar police commissionerate stated that firefighting efforts continued under the supervision of the chief fire officer. Initial reports suggested a short circuit triggered the fire, but the exact cause remains unconfirmed. Further information on damage and the cause was awaited.
items.title: Fire breaks out at Noida hotel and spreads to nearby eateries

items.summary: Anusua Mukherjee, Deputy Editor of Frontline, reviews the 2024 book 'A History of Ghosts, Spirits and the Supernatural' by discussing its illustrations and content. She recounts childhood stories about a ghost named Kamri and connects the book's themes to her interest in horror. Mukherjee highlights specific entities like Pazuzu and scarab beetles, noting their cultural significance. She references an interview with author Kuzhali Manickavel, who argues that supernatural entities are not metaphors but unexplainable realities. The review concludes with Mukherjee's anticipation of receiving her copy of Manickavel's novel.
items.title: Anusua Mukherjee Reviews a Book on Supernatural Entities

items.summary: Ahead of her memoir 'Belonging' release on November 10, Sonia Gandhi posted on X recalling her first meeting with Rajiv Gandhi at a Greek restaurant in Cambridge. She described him as very good-looking and gentle, noting they met through a common friend. Her debut post included a video where she shared memories of their relationship, which began in that Cambridge eatery frequented by students.
items.title: Sonia Gandhi Recalls First Meeting With Rajiv Gandhi Ahead of Memoir Release

items.summary: Kotak Mahindra Bank reported a 29% year-on-year increase in standalone profit to Rs 4,212 crore in Q2FY27. Net interest income rose 16% to Rs 8,459 crore. Consolidated customer assets grew 21% to Rs 6,99,250 crore as of September 30, 2026. The bank also saw a 16% rise in book value per share to Rs 196. Share prices declined 1.49% on the NSE.
items.title: Kotak Mahindra Bank Reports Strong Q2 Profit Growth

items.summary: Indian equity markets declined across all four sessions of a holiday-shortened week, with the Nifty 50 closing 2.4% lower at 22,600. Foreign investors sold equities worth a net Rs 26,970 crore, a significant drop from the previous week's outflows, while domestic institutional investors remained net buyers for the 10th consecutive week, purchasing Rs 1,09,420 crore. Despite this support, mid- and small-cap stocks faced heavy selling pressure due to concerns over crude oil prices, inflation, and global monetary policy. Analysts note that while large caps held up, the technical structure has deteriorated, with key moving averages under pressure. The Nifty's outlook remains uncertain as investors await global central bank decisions and domestic data.
items.title: FIIs Continue Selling Indian Stocks Amid Market Slide

items.summary: A review describes Amal Singh's novel Slow Burn as an inventive coming-of-age story blending urban fantasy, magic realism, and noir. The plot follows Rishi Tripathi, a struggling actor in Mumbai who, after a humiliating audition, punches a mirror and falls into an alternate reality where he is a successful Bollywood star. The narrative explores the dark side of ambition and the cost of success, revealing that the protagonist's doppelganger was displaced from this ideal world. The reviewer notes the book's seamless blend of genres and its slow-burn pacing, though they mention the doppelganger reveal feels slightly rushed in the final third. Published by Penguin India, the novel is set against a backdrop of familiar Bollywood nostalgia.
items.title: Review of Amal Singh's Slow Burn Urban Fantasy Novel

items.summary: Activists in Arunachal Pradesh face detention and intimidation regarding the Siang Upper Multipurpose project. On October 9, police detained four activists from Geku village under the Arunachal Pradesh Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 2014, to contain unlawful activities. Residents allege the government has militarized villages, blocked social media, and threatened officials to suppress opposition to the 11,000 MW dam. While the government claims the project protects against a larger Chinese dam, villagers argue their ancestral lands face submersion. Authorities filed at least 40 FIRs since 2025, and village headmen report suspensions due to protests. Chief Minister Pema Khandu defended the measures, stating those disrupting law and order would be dealt with according to the law.
items.title: Arunachal Government Faces Protests Over Proposed Dam Amidst Detentions
